reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, round-6 rounding-fix verification

samples_reviewed.question_text: An object's mass measures 15 g. About how many g is that, rounded to the nearest 10?
An object's mass measures 5 g. About how many g is that, rounded to the nearest 10?
An object's mass measures 53 g. About how many g is that, rounded to the nearest 10?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Hand-checked all 10 rendered answer keys by round-half-up: the prior seed-43 defect (5 g keyed to 0) is gone -- 5 g now keys to 10, and the paired midpoint case 35 g still correctly keys to 40, so both exact-midpoint samples now agree on rounding up rather than one going down and one going up.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The lc text names three units, 'grams, kilograms, and/or milligrams', but this 10-sample batch is exclusively grams (5 g to 64 g); no kilogram or milligram magnitude appears, so unit breadth cannot be confirmed from this batch alone.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Each item is a single two-clause sentence stating a given mass and asking for its nearest-10 value, e.g. 'An object's mass measures 41 g...', which is a short, single-step arithmetic task fitting grade-3 quarter-2 reading load.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The 10 magnitudes span both rounding directions and the boundary case: values needing round-down (41, 64, 32), round-up from below-half (46, 9), an exact tens multiple (10), and two true midpoints (5, 35), giving a well-distributed sample of the round-half-up rule rather than only easy cases.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every item hands the student an exact known measurement and asks only for its rounded value, which is a place-value rounding skill; the lc's own vocab term 'estimate mass' implies judging an unmeasured object's mass by benchmark or comparison, a distinct skill this batch never actually samples.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Gram magnitudes here run from 5 to 64, a small two-digit range that stays well within what a grade-3 quarter-2 learner would plausibly encounter for a single handheld object's mass.
